articles.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-5 with Extended Reasoning and Native Multimodal Generation
articles.summary: OpenAI officially released GPT-5 in mid-July 2026, featuring substantially improved long-horizon reasoning, native image and audio generation, and a unified architecture that collapses what were previously separate models into a single system. Benchmarks show significant gains on graduate-level science, mathematics, and agentic coding tasks, with the model able to sustain coherent multi-step plans across sessions lasting hours.

articles.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Ultra 2 Achieves New State-of-the-Art on Scientific Research Benchmarks
articles.summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini Ultra 2, which sets new records on FrontierMath and GPQA Diamond benchmarks, solving problems previously considered out of reach for AI systems. The model integrates a refined mixture-of-experts architecture with improved tool use, enabling it to autonomously write and execute verification code during complex reasoning chains.

articles.title: Tesla Optimus Begins Limited Deployment in Third-Party Warehouses
articles.summary: Tesla confirmed that its Optimus Gen-3 humanoid robots have started operating in select third-party logistics and warehousing facilities beyond Tesla's own factories. The robots handle box sorting, palletizing, and inventory scanning, with Tesla reporting sustained 18-hour operational cycles between charges. The deployment marks the first commercial sale of Optimus units outside Tesla's internal operations.

articles.title: Figure AI Demonstrates Conversational Multi-Robot Coordination in BMW Assembly Line
articles.summary: Figure AI released footage and technical details of its Figure 02 robots coordinating tasks on a BMW assembly line using natural language instructions relayed from a central AI planner. The system allows a human supervisor to issue high-level goals that are automatically decomposed into subtasks and distributed across multiple robots in real time, reducing manual programming overhead dramatically.

articles.title: Anthropic Introduces Claude's Computer Use 2.0 with Autonomous Multi-App Workflows
articles.summary: Anthropic rolled out a major upgrade to Claude's computer use capabilities, allowing the model to autonomously navigate complex multi-application workflows across desktop and web environments with significantly improved reliability. The system now supports persistent browser sessions, file management, and chained API calls, positioning it as a practical AI agent for enterprise back-office automation.

articles.title: TSMC Begins Volume Production of 1.4nm Process Node Ahead of Schedule
articles.summary: TSMC announced that its N1.4 process node has entered volume production at its Fab 20 complex in Tainan, approximately one quarter ahead of the originally projected timeline. The node delivers a roughly 20% performance improvement and 30% power reduction over N2, and is expected to power next-generation AI accelerators and mobile SoCs shipping in early 2027.

articles.title: Neuralink Receives FDA Clearance for Second-Generation Brain-Computer Interface Implant
articles.summary: The FDA granted clearance for Neuralink's N2 implant, a second-generation brain-computer interface featuring 4x the electrode count of its predecessor, wireless high-bandwidth data streaming, and a simplified surgical insertion procedure. Early clinical trial participants with spinal cord injuries demonstrated cursor control speeds approaching able-bodied benchmarks, marking a significant milestone for assistive neurotechnology.

articles.title: Boston Dynamics and Hyundai Unveil Atlas Commercial Platform for Construction Sites
articles.summary: Boston Dynamics, backed by Hyundai, officially launched the commercial version of its electric Atlas humanoid robot tailored for construction environments. The platform features ruggedized hardware, dust and water resistance rated at IP67, and an SDK that allows construction firms to program site-specific inspection, material transport, and documentation tasks. Pilot programs are underway with three major general contractors in the U.S. and South Korea.
